title: Tenant communication playlet — fallthrough decision cards (draft)
content:
Purpose: quick customer-facing playlet (short, modular pieces) to power status-page updates + post-incident summary for tenants affected by the 2028-04-02 fallthrough event. Goal is to give customers clear choices, verifiable evidence, and a concise timeline they can act on. This is a working draft — lots of TODOs and placeholders below (marked).

High-level one-liner for status page (initial):
- We observed an intermittent model fallthrough affecting a subset of requests in EU region (2028-04-02 02:10–03:40 UTC). We’ve applied routing mitigations and are validating responses; some tenants may see partial or stale outputs.

Short update for status page (update 1 — mitigation applied):
- Mitigation: traffic was re-routed to a compatible model variant with preserved KV cache semantics at 02:45 UTC; rate-limited burst queueing in eu-west-1 disabled for affected pools. Visible recovery for many tenants observed by 03:05 UTC. Investigating full integrity of responses.

Final closure blurb (status page final):
- Incident resolved: full routing and cache integrity checks completed by 04:00 UTC. No evidence of data loss. Affected tenants will receive a post-incident summary and optional evidence bundle on request.

Customer-facing postmortem skeleton (short):
1) What happened (plain language):
- Between 02:10 and 03:40 UTC, a service-level regression in the routing component caused requests to be delivered to a model variant with an incompatible LRU cache policy. This produced occasional truncated/mis-ordered structured outputs for roughly 1.7% of requests in the impacted pool.

2) Who was affected:
- Scope: tenants using hosted inference in eu-west-1 on the following routes: /v1/chat (model tag: rwd-1b-q8), /v1/generate (tenant tagged pools A/B). Estimated impacted requests: ~12k over the window.

3) Customer impact (what customers would see):
- Symptoms: truncated JSON objects in streaming sessions, missing trailing tokens in some chat sessions, and occasional small mis-ordering of list elements returned by reranking. Most errors returned HTTP 500 or 206 depending on streaming cut.

4) Immediate mitigations performed:
- Automated reroute to rwd-1b-q8-compatible variant at 02:45 UTC.
- KV cache flush + prefix revalidation on affected nodes (02:50–02:58 UTC).
- Added temporary conservative timeout and disabled continuous batching for the impacted pool (03:00 UTC).
- Customer-facing actions: posted interim status, opened dedicated support thread for tenants showing evidence of corruption.

5) Evidence and verification offered to tenants:
- We will provide a downloadable evidence bundle per tenant on request: includes request IDs, server-side traces (scrubbed), token-level diffs where available, and signed checksums of responses before/after mitigation.
- Verification steps tenants can perform locally: replay sample request IDs via our replay endpoint (instructions attached below).

6) Short-term follow-ups (next 72 hrs):
- SRE: run full cache-coherence sweep in eu-west clusters and publish integrity report (owner: Diego, due 2028-04-06).
- Serving-runtime: revert the aggressive kernel-selection change that triggered the incompatible cache behavior and add unit tests for LRU policy (owner: Samir, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1842, due 2028-04-07).
- Product: open a tenant opt-in for automated replay and proof bundles (owner: Priya, due 2028-04-06).

7) Long-term fixes (quarter roadmap items):
- Harden model-variant compatibility matrix and validate cache semantics at canary time.
- Add a per-tenant verification job that samples responses post-rollout for regression detection.
- Improve status message templating to include clear tenant action links and evidence request button.

Decision cards (what to offer each tenant — short, pick one):
- Card A — Automatic replay and reconcile (recommended): we will replay impacted requests against the verified post-mitigation model and provide a reconciliation report + token diffs. Opt-in required. Expected time: 24–72 hrs depending on volume.
- Card B — Manual evidence bundle + engineer walkthrough: we provide the evidence bundle and schedule a 30m call to walk through artifacts.
- Card C — Accept incident/monitor: no action; confirm you received notice and our integrity checks.
- Card D — Request SLA credit + formal audit package: for enterprise tenants wanting a compliance-grade artifact (may require a formal request and NDAs).

Templates for short customer emails / support thread posts (pick and adapt):
- Short notify (support thread):
  Hi <tenant-team>,

  We observed a partial degradation impacting some requests in eu-west-1 on 2028-04-02. We have applied routing mitigations and validated most traffic; however, if you see any truncated or missing tokens please reply to this thread and choose one of the attached remediation options (automatic replay, evidence bundle + call, or no-action).

  We can provide request-level evidence. If you want the automatic replay, say: "OPT-IN REPLAY" and we will queue it.

  — Maya (Customer Success)

- Sample statuspage note for tenants who opted in to replay:
  We are replaying your queued requests now; we will post the reconciliation report and token-diff package to your tenant support folder when complete.

Replay instructions for tenants (how to verify):
- Use the replay endpoint: POST https://api.redwood.ai/internal/replay with body {"tenant_id":"<tenant>", "request_ids":[...]} (support will pre-fill for tenant).
- Replies include: original_response_checksum, replay_response_checksum, token_diff (if present). Checksums are signed by Redwood KMS.
- If you want a live walkthrough, reply with: "WALKTHROUGH" and we will schedule a 30m slot.

Open questions / TO DOs in this draft:
- Confirm exact list of impacted tenant_ids and whether any enterprise tenants need separate legal workflows (Priya owns).
- Decide whether we auto-opt-in low-volume tenants for replay vs. require explicit consent (policy decision: product + legal).
- Finalize evidence bundle scrub policy (PII redaction checklist) and SLA for bundle delivery.
- Pull exact counts by route + per-tenant QPS impact for the customer-facing appendix (data team).

Appendix (technical summary for interested customers):
- Root cause (short): an untested change in kernel selection logic modified eviction timing in the KV cache under high prefix-collision workloads, causing mismatch in prefix alignment for some streaming sessions. The change passed unit-level perf tests but lacked an integration check for LRU semantics across model variants.
- Why mitigation worked: rerouting to a variant with compatible KV semantics removed the mismatch and allowed cached prefixes to align; cache flush removed the inconsistent prefixes so subsequent requests returned stable outputs.
- Risk of recurrence: low if kernel-selection change is reverted and new integration tests added; medium until we have canary sampling in production.

Contact and next steps for customers who need urgent help:
- For evidence bundle requests or replay opt-in: reply in-thread or email cs-mitigation@redwood.ai with subject: "Replay request — <tenant> — INC-2028-04".
- Emergency escalation (enterprise): cc the assigned TAM or open Priority support case with keyword: "ESCALATE-INC-2028-04".

Sign-off and versioning:
- Draft author: Maya Chen (CS) 2028-04-03
- Draft reviewers: Diego, Priya, Samir (2028-04-04)
- Next edit: incorporate exact tenant list and attach sample evidence bundle (2028-04-05).

Notes to internal reviewers (not for customer):
- Keep language plain; avoid tech jargon like "KV drift" when sending to non-technical contacts.
- Legal: check the wording for "no evidence of data loss" vs. "no customer data was deleted" — legal prefers the latter for enterprise notices.
- Ops: confirm the replay endpoint rate limits for bulk tenant replays (SRE owns gating).

--- End of playlet draft ---
